title: Growing without soil
subtitle: A classroom hydroponics project
intro: We’re building a classroom garden. First, we have to get the water moving.
question: What does a plant need when we take away the soil?
now: The frame and lights are up. We’re connecting four pairs of growing channels to one pump and reservoir.
next: Finish the tubing. Check for leaks. Test the flow through all four routes.
modelNote: Based on classroom photos. Dimensions and planting-hole spacing are approximate. Tubing shows the intended layout.

phases.title: Define & build
phases.description: Identify plant needs and compare designs against space, cost, and maintenance constraints.
phases.activity: Investigate food and land use, visit a garden, assign system jobs, then sketch and build a prototype.
phases.evidence: A design sketch and an explanation of why the chosen system meets the constraints.

phases.title: Move the water
phases.description: Explain how the pump, height, slope, and fittings affect water movement.
phases.activity: Model branching with tees. Connect the four paired routes, check for leaks, and measure flow while changing one variable.
phases.evidence: A labeled water-path diagram and before-and-after flow measurements.

phases.title: Light & living plants
phases.description: Connect photosynthesis and cellular respiration to plant growth.
phases.activity: Use the slideshow and companion worksheet. Germinate lettuce, transplant seedlings, and compare light conditions.
phases.evidence: A plant observation log and an explanation of how light supports growth.

phases.title: Mix & measure
phases.description: Explain solutions, nutrients, and pH, and connect water conditions to plant health.
phases.activity: Mix nutrient solution, practice measurement, and compare changes in pH or concentration under teacher guidance.
phases.evidence: A measurement record and a cause-and-effect explanation.

phases.title: Keep the system healthy
phases.description: Trace matter through the system and recognize disturbances over time.
phases.activity: Track growth and water use. Diagnose problems such as algae or blocked drainage and document a response.
phases.evidence: A claim supported by observations and data from the system.

phases.title: Improve & share
phases.description: Use evidence to improve the design and evaluate sustainability trade-offs.
phases.activity: Revise the system, compare hydroponics with soil growing, and prepare a demonstration, poster, or presentation. Harvest when ready.
phases.evidence: A design defense and reflection on what changed, why it changed, and what the evidence shows.
